clue.text: One of the family is boarding

definitions.meaning: a relative by a parent's remarriage, a husband's or wife's male child
read as a phrase, puts a foot onto, as a passenger climbing aboard a vehicle

explanation.surface: A relative is staying somewhere as a boarder.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words, STEPS ON, to get the second sense: getting on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepchild is a family member by marriage; stepping on a bus or train is boarding it.

clue.text: Port holds the western answer in the main

indicators.note: the western answer is placed in the middle of the word for the main

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: A harbour town keeps the answer from the west out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old literary name for the sea, a crossword favourite. SWANSEA is a port city in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a Welsh coastal city with docks, an example of a harbour town.

clue.text: Copy to rivet attention

definitions.meaning: in law, to write out a document in a large formal hand, producing a fair copy

explanation.surface: Imitating something to hold people's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a legal one: a clerk would engross a deed by writing out its final copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk transcribing a deed in final form engrosses it; a gripping book absorbs its reader wholly.

clue.text: The setting for some confrontation

definitions.meaning: the place where a story or event happens
a noisy public row, as in making a fuss in a restaurant

explanation.surface: Describing the location chosen for a showdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some confrontation' points at the idiom of making a fuss in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's location is its backdrop, and a public outburst or row is called making one.

clue.text: No rocky situation — before debts become widely known

indicators.note: the rocky hill comes earlier in the answer than the debts

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, a common feature of English moorland
IOUs are written promises to repay, so debts

explanation.surface: No precarious state should come before your debts are made public.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky peak, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England. IOUS, plural of IOU (I owe you), stands for debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous, usually for something bad, so known by many people.

clue.text: Regain health but take out extra insurance?

definitions.meaning: to get better after an illness
to cover again, hyphenated as ..., taking out a further policy

explanation.surface: Someone getting well but also buying more insurance just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading RE-COVER: insurance gives cover, so more insurance covers you again.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient getting better is on the mend; insurers provide cover, so a second policy covers again.

clue.text: Speedily made an artist joke mounts

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: in a down clue the joke climbs upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pun is a joke on a word's two senses

explanation.surface: A painter's quip keeps climbing in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounts' means the joke reads upwards, giving NUP. To run up a dress is to sew it quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up clothes or a bill is to produce or rack it up rapidly.

clue.text: A firm sister beat the problem

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a nun is a religious sister
to beat is to drum, as on a drum or a table

explanation.surface: A company and a nun tackled the difficulty head-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a puzzling question or riddle, a difficulty to be solved.

clue.text: Church authority in the forefront at one hundred

indicators.note: the words at one hundred go inside the forefront

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the front of an army or movement
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A church body leading the way when a centenary arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vatican is the Pope's seat of government in Rome, so the authority of the Roman Catholic Church.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal government in Rome is the governing power of the Catholic faith.

clue.text: Soldiers stand over the crowd and keep under control

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldiers sit above the crowd, so they come first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a press is a dense throng of people

explanation.surface: Troops stationed above a mob keep order.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a standard crossword shorthand for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress feelings or a revolt is to hold them down or restrain them.

clue.text: Add something — a grated nutmeg possibly

indicators.note: grated nutmeg is broken into pieces, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sprinkle a little grated nutmeg on top, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grated' signals rearranging the seven letters of A NUTMEG; 'possibly' is part of the cookery picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase something by adding to it.

clue.text: Express this in a single sentence!

definitions.text: Express this in a single sentence!

parts.words: Express this in a single sentence!
parts.note: an express train makes no halts, and a single long sentence runs without a full stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' is the fast train, and the punctuation reading imagines a sentence with no full stop in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An express service runs without halting, just as one long sentence runs with no full stop.

clue.text: A fleshy-leaved plant producing weighty harvest

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds
a crop is what is harvested

explanation.surface: A succulent that gives a heavy yield.
explanation.walkthrough: A STONE is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedum, a low succulent of rocks and walls, has thick juicy leaves.

clue.text: Critical about hard though most suitable position

indicators.note: the word for critical goes around the letter for hard

parts.note: nice in its old sense means finely discriminating or fastidious
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Being fussy about difficulty, but this is the ideal spot.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE here has its older meaning of precise or exacting, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is the role or place that suits someone ideally.

clue.text: A supplement is for the recess

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a supplement added to a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extra item is intended for the alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: APSIS is an alternative form of apse, the vaulted recess at the end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular alcove in a church, so a recess.

clue.text: He objects to laying out money for a hide of stone

definitions.text: He objects to laying out money

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: A man who refuses to pay for a leather made of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laying out' means spending here, not arranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hates parting with cash, refusing to spend.

clue.text: Gifts of iron hoops

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
rings are hoops

explanation.surface: Presents of iron hoops.
explanation.definitionFit: Offerings are things given, such as donations or presents.

clue.text: A bird taken as picnic food?

definitions.meaning: a large thrush that visits Britain in winter
read as two words, food eaten out in a field, as at a picnic

explanation.surface: A bird served up as a meal in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as FIELD FARE: 'fare' is food, and a picnic is eaten in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a thrush species; fare is food and a picnic happens outdoors on grass.

clue.text: Unduly put out when in charge of the children

parts.note: being over something means supervising it
issue is offspring, a person's children

explanation.surface: Upset when looking after the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like annoyed, but it means distributed: to overissue is to print or release too many.
explanation.definitionFit: To overissue shares or banknotes is to release more than is allowed or wise.

clue.text: Verbose characters, say

indicators.note: the letters of verbose are treated as loose characters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Wordy people, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link meaning 'for example', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to remark or comment.

clue.text: Total wipe-out is certain after a time

indicators.note: the word for certain is placed after the time period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Complete destruction is guaranteed in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a complete rubbing out or removal.

clue.text: It's worth making time about mid-afternoon

indicators.note: the letters are turned about, mixed into a fresh order
mid- points to the central letter of the word afternoon

explanation.surface: Something valuable is earned by putting in hours around mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-' gives R, the middle of AFTERNOON; 'about' mixes TIME plus R into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is value or excellence deserving reward.

clue.text: Stood up and scoffed, looking quite pink

parts.note: rose means got to one's feet
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone got up after eating and looked rather flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' means gobbled food (British slang), not mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rose-coloured, a fairly pink tint.

clue.text: To let a thousand in can cause distress

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the thousand is placed in the middle of the word for let

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Renting out a property for a thousand can be upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To let' looks like a property sign, but TO stays as written and only 'let' becomes RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is great suffering or anguish.

clue.text: Employees getting support

definitions.meaning: a stick or pole to lean on

explanation.surface: Workers getting a helping hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's workforce is its personnel; a walking stick or pole holds someone up.

clue.text: A restorer dealing with furniture for storage

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a dresser is a cabinet with shelves and drawers

explanation.surface: A furniture restorer working on a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Latin for 'in the matter of', means about or concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts things right again, setting a wrong straight.

clue.text: A jolly fellow no longer up the pole — at sea

definitions.text: A jolly fellow no longer up the pole — at sea

parts.words: A jolly fellow no longer up the pole — at sea
parts.note: the pirates' skull-and-crossbones flag, a jolly chap's name, is no longer hoisted on ships' masts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' and the name complete the pirate flag's name; 'up the pole' means flown from the mast, not crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name which, after 'Jolly', names the old pirate flag once flown on masts.

clue.text: Appear hesitant, right or wrong

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seeming unsure whether something is right or wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something done amiss.

clue.text: Out in the arena inflicting defeat

indicators.note: the word out is placed inside the word for the arena

parts.note: a ring is an arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: Knocking someone out in the arena, beating them.
explanation.definitionFit: Routing an army means defeating it utterly and putting it to flight.

clue.text: Area where one keeps changing gear

indicators.note: the word for one holds the rearranged letters within it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: changing gear shifts the letters of gear to a new order

explanation.surface: A place where someone keeps shifting gears in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' scrambles gear into REAG, and 'keeps' holds that inside the card word; 'where' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land extent measured in acres.

clue.text: Choose gold for a royal personage

parts.note: to elect is to choose
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Picking gold for a member of the royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: An Elector was a German prince entitled to help choose the Holy Roman Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Electors were princes of the Holy Roman Empire who voted for the emperor.

clue.text: Listening equipment may be sent, and that's serious

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: may be signals the letters of sent could be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Hearing aids may be posted off, and that is no joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' scrambles the word sent into NEST; 'and that's' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and solemn in intent.
